title: Ashes of Ariandel
snippet:
Ashes of Ariandel -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : Due to a logistical error, *Ashes of Ariandel* was released early for a short period of time on October 21st, 2016, for Season Pass owners on Xbox One. This accidental release forced the company to reschedule the release date for Steam and PlayStation 4 to October 24th, instead of the originally planned October 25th for all consoles.

snippet:
Ashes of Ariandel -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : ***Ashes of Ariandel*** is downloadable content for the game *Dark Souls III*. It was released on October 21st, 2016 for Xbox One, and on October 24th, 2016 for PlayStation 4 and PC.

Its cost on release was $14.99, or it could be downloaded with the Season Pass.

It is the first of two expansions, the other being *The Ringed City*.

title: Birch Woman
snippet:
Birch Woman -  Dark Souls III - enemy - birch_woman_cryomancer 
 birch_woman_cryomancer : This type of Birch Woman is especially dangerous because, as they have no fireballs attached to their branches, they blend perfectly in the environment. It attacks silently with a flood of ice that inflicts Frostbite build-up and a fairly high damage. It can also stretch its branches to strike the player from a distance.

Versions of this enemy that use both forms of combat are located in the Depths of The Painting.

title: Birch Woman
snippet:
Birch Woman -  Dark Souls III - enemy - notes 
 notes : Fireballs are affected by Alluring Skulls.
There is a Birch Woman who guards the Snap Freeze spell that seems to be more aggressive than the rest.

title: Birch Woman
snippet:
Another suggested strategy is throwing an Alluring Skull down on the earth. The fireballs cast by the Birch Woman Pyromancer will follow the skull instead of the player, allowing the player to attack safely.

For those who prefer archery, they are easily dealt with from a long distance (farther than their attack range, especially with the Hawk Ring) with either a crossbow or bow.

title: Birch Woman
snippet:
Birch Woman -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The real threat provided by these enemies is their camouflage. It is possible to determine whether a Birch Woman is dangerous by looking directly at the hair on their heads. If the hair stands still, it is not an enemy, but if it move slightly because of the wind, then it is an enemy.

Even though they are slow enemies, they must not be underestimated because they are often found near other faster enemies, such as Wolves. They provide ranged support for these enemies, and can be problematic if not dealt with.

As soon as a Birch Woman is recognized, the player can simply run and kill it. The player shouldn't be greedy; attack them from behind, as to prevent their grab attack. In about three to four hits they should be down. If they are hit with Fire damage, they will catch fire and scream, becoming incapacitated.

title: Birch Woman
snippet:
Birch Woman -  Dark Souls III - enemy - birch_woman_pyromancer 
 birch_woman_pyromancer : This White Tree can be identified by the little fireballs lying on its branches. It will unleash these fireballs if triggered and they will follow the player until they strike them or a solid surface. If all fireballs reach the player, they will inflict a noticeable amount of damage or a heavy stamina drain.

title: Birch Woman
snippet:
Birch Woman -  Dark Souls III - enemy - description 
 description : Birch Women are silent enemies that resemble a tree with feminine features that blend themselves into the environment. They are, in fact, trees, but are capable of slowly moving and attack in different ways. If the player is not in their aggro range, they will stand still and, even if triggered, they will attack silently, better from behind the player's shoulders, trying not to be located. Indeed, sometimes it can be hard to locate one of them because they are almost perfectly camouflaged in the wilderness.

Near the first bonfire there are some non-hostile specimens.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: The Gravetender will walk up after a short time (his footprints will be visible through the fog). Once he is there, cast Poison or Toxic Mist again, until his health bar begins to shrink. Be aware that he can shoot sorceries through the fog and they can hit you. Once he is dead, in order to spawn the Greatwolf, you have to make your way all the way up to the chapel (warping via a bonfire resets the fight) and down into the basement with the Giant Flies until the howl of the Greatwolf is heard, then run all the way back to the fog wall of the boss fight, and repeat the cheese on the wolf as with the Gravetender. However, since the trip is long and arduous and the flies are particularly dangerous, you can just enter the fog after the man dies (the prompt appears when close to it) and deal with the wolf in normal combat. The wolf will appear near the building, as soon as the fog wall is entered.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: The ideal strategy during the second phase is to try to finish off the Gravetender as quickly as possible, to remove the Greatwolf's support and ensure that there is only one enemy to focus on. A good tactic to minimize exposure to the Greatwolf's attacks is to lure it around the pillars of the large tower in the arena; this works particularly well against its charging attacks as the pillars provide cover against them as well as deflecting the Greatwolf away from the player. This can allow the player to avoid the Greatwolf's attacks, and buy time to maneuver around to engage the Gravetender alone.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Long ago, an Undead declared a tournament in which their fellow cursed souls would battle to the repeated death, with their worth being measured in deaths. This was seen as a gift to the Undead, who go hollow without a purpose, and a fight with no end was considered by some to be a glorious use of their immortality.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : It is advised to kill the three wolves that accompany the Champion's Gravetender at the beginning of the fight as to ensure they do not become problematic when facing him head on. The Gravetender will fight very aggressively, using his sword and shield's unique combination attacks to strike while blocking, turning each attempt to attack him into a trade that minimizes damage to himself. For this reason, it is not suggested to use small arms such as straight swords to fight him, but rather to use bigger weapons such as an ultra greatsword to inflict heavy stagger on him and to break his guard to open him up to ripostes. He is weak against Lightning and Bleed, which might be good to keep in mind.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: They will only be relieved of their duty by the Ashen One, who finds their way to the bottom of the painting and challenges the duo to partake in the old turnament of the champion. Should they not do that, however, the fate of the page and wolf remains a mystery. All that is known is that the old champion's remains would find their way in the possession of Amnesiac Lapp during the collapse of the world into the Dreg Heap.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: The Gravetender Greatwolf can actually be found earlier on in two different locations. The first of them is at the end of a forested field full of wolves, found beyond the collapsing snow shelf. The second one is found as the player proceeds uphill past the ruined tower guarded by Millwood Knights.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: Once the Gravetender Greatwolf joins the fight, the enemy will bring out a Sorcerer's Staff and start using spells like Great Soul Arrow and Snap Freeze more often to support his beastly enforcer from a distance, switching back to his sword and shield should the player get too close.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - exploit 
 exploit : It is possible to cheese the fight against the boss: from the Depths of the Painting bonfire, approach the ledge around the arena, but do not hop down. Instead, equip the Black Bow of Pharis and the Hawk Ring, plus Feather Arrows. The bow paired with the ring and standard arrows doesn't work for the cheese, as they don't go far enough. Zoom in and there will be a wolf visible to the right, next to a column. Shoot at it to aggro it and the fog wall will appear. Step back at this point and cast poison Mist or Toxic Mist around the area where you just stood. Three wolves at the base of the short cliff will get poisoned and their diminishing health bars will appear visible behind the wall.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - plot 
 plot : The Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf are an easy to miss optional encounter found within the *Ashes of Ariandel DLC*.

The fight starts off with just the Champion's Gravetender and three wolves. Once his health has been halved, he will call for the Greatwolf by performing the "By my sword" gesture, making the fight a lot more challenging. Defeating both enemies here allows the player to obtain the Champion's Bones. By burning them at the bonfire in Firelink Shrine, they'll be able to unlock the Undead Match, a type of PvP mode. Beating the boss also results in obtaining Valorheart, which could be the player's only reward if they've somehow found the Champion's Bones already by exploring *The Ringed City DLC* first.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: The Greatwolf, on the other hand, fights very aggressively and will perform a charging attack very similar to that of Vordt of the Boreal Valley, albeit much faster. It's not advised to block these attacks with anything less than a greatshield, as they can devastate the player's stamina, leading to a guard break and an almost guaranteed hit from the Greatwolf. Once the Greatwolf is at 50% health, it will perform a howl and its eyes will glow red. At this point the Greatwolf gains a Frost breath attack and becomes even faster and more aggressive. It shares the same weaknesses to Lightning and Bleed as its master, with an added Fire weakness. Most of these strategies also apply to its solo appearances outside the boss fight, though one must be aware of the amount of normal wolves that may turn the tides in the beast's favor in those situations.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : The and the are an optional duo boss in the *Dark Souls III: Ashes of Ariandel DLC*. The Greatwolf also appears as a powerful enemy outside of the designated boss fight.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: location : The boss fight is found in an optional location of the Painted World of Ariandel. The player must destroy the rickety bridge that leads to the chapel from the side of said chapel, which will then allow them to climb down using the bridge's remains, like in the Catacombs of Carthus. From there, they must descend using the large roots jutting out of the cliffside, fending off Farron Followers and avoiding the exploding arrows that are shot by the two Millwood Knights below. After reaching the bottom, one can find the Depths of the Painting bonfire by proceeding forward from the last root where one of the Millwood Knights stood. From there, the boss fight can be reached by turning right and dropping down into the flower field opposite from the side of the frozen lake with Frost Crabs. The Champion's Gravetender will be found beneath a building resembling Crossbreed Priscilla's old battle arena from *Dark Souls*.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: The Champion of the Undead Match eventually went mad, ending up in the Painted World of Ariandel as a result. Only his page and a large wolf stayed by his side, until the day he finally died. The champion was buried in the lower section of the painting, where a small tombstone is still guarded by the very same page and wolf that had remained with him in his madness. They became guardians of that place, learning to utilize the frost that permeated that land as a way to uphold their task. The Greatwolf quickly established itself as the leader among the other wolves as well, commanding them and likely using them as guards of the tomb as well.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : The word "**大狼**", which means a "Great Wolf", was also used in *Dark Souls* as part of Sif's title.
The translation of the Greatwolf's name may cause a bit of confusion: the Greatwolf is just a pet of the Gravetender, not a Gravetender itself.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Unlike the Gravetender, who remains in the arena at all times, the Greatwolf can be encountered earlier on as a powerful miniboss-like encounter, fighting alongside a rather numerous pack of smaller wolves. It has the same abilities as in the boss battle, but unlike in that fight, its health must not be depleated fully, as it will flee after less than half of it has been removed.

If the player defeats the Greatwolf in these two encounters, they will receive three Large Titanite Shard with each victory. This also has the added bonus of lowering its boss fight health by 10% with each time it is beaten.The effect will not reset if the player dies on their first attempt of the boss battle, meaning it is permanently weakened. Beating it with the Gravetender before defeating it in the other areas of Ariandel will make it disappear from those locations, meaning the Large Titanite Shards cannot be obtained any longer.

title: Corvian Knight
snippet:
Corvian Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - description 
 description : Corvian Knights are tall avian warriors that tower over their lesser brethren and are considerably more intelligent and fearsome. They exist in two variations, one that wears a hooded robe and wields the Crow Quills, and a naked variant that wields the Crow Talons.

They can be encountered throughout the Corvian Settlement exterminating other Forlorn Corvians, although they will quickly turn their attention to the player.

title: Corvian Knight
snippet:
Corvian Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - lore 
 lore : Corvian Knights presumably protected the Corvian Settlement and its inhabitants within the Painted World of Ariandel. Whenever a Painting begins to rot, those who settled within it resolve to burn it away in order to give way for the creation of a new one. When the Corvians were faced with this event, they were prepared to burn it. However, after Sister Friede arrived in the Painting, the Corvian Knights became infatuated with her, choosing to loyally serve her and assist in her mission to let the world rot instead. To that end, the Corvian Knights betrayed their brethren, and their loyalty to Friede was so devout that they willingly slaughtered their own kin if they were perceived to be a threat.

title: Corvian Knight
snippet:
Corvian Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : Crow Talons-wielding Corvian Knights can perform an attack similar to that of Crow Demons, where they jump onto the back of the player and start pecking at their faces.

title: Corvian Knight
snippet:
Corvian Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Corvian Knights are incredibly agile opponents and will regularly backflip away or leap over the player to disorient them, often following up with a lunging stab. This can be punished by dodging and backstabbing. Their flurry of blade attacks can rapidly inflict bleed, even when guarding through a shield, so it's not recommended to attempt to block their strikes. From a distance, they will throw several knives and will often perform this attack if the player attempts to heal or use an item.

The robed Corvian Knights will pursue and eliminate the lesser Corvians around the settlement, although they will focus on the player if alerted. The variant wielding talons is often encountered hiding upside down under bridges and ceilings, so it is advisable for the player to be mindful of their surroundings.

title: Crow Quills
snippet:
Crow Quills -  Dark Souls III - weapon - availability 
 availability : From the Corvian Settlement bonfire, head out and across the bridge. Follow the wall of the house on your left until you see a smaller bridge. Go across and follow the path to the left. On your left you will see two entrances across a small gap. Jump it and go into the house on your right. Barrels will be blocking a platform that you need to run and leap off of and land on the elevated platform with the Crow Quills.

title: Crow Quills
snippet: Scaling primarily with Dexterity, this weapon's one-handed attacks are the same as that of normal thrusting swords. However, when two-handed, rather than holding the weapon in both hands, the wielder will brandish a set of blades in the off-hand and use them to perform combination attacks. Whereas most thrusting swords have narrow poking attacks that are aimed forward, the Crow Quills allows the wielder to use the blades for slashing attacks, providing wider horizontal coverage than a thrusting sword is normally capable of. This gives the Crow Quills a rather versatile moveset in which the left-handed blades can cover for the right-handed sword's weaknesses. Of special note, the two-handed running attack provides Hyper Armor to the wielder, something that no other thrusting sword is capable of doing.

title: Crow Quills
snippet: The Crow Quills also possesses a unique skill in that the off-hand blades can be thrown in a fan-shaped pattern while leaping in the air. This grants the wielder a form of ranged damage while performing an evasive maneuver, which can be a useful tool in the hands of crafty players.

title: Crow Talons
snippet:
Crow Talons -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Crow Talons have the same moveset as the Claws, with the exception of the two-handed rolling and running attacks. The running attack is comparable to the weapon art Onislayer, being a jump and cross slash. If used while running off a ledge, it will automatically transition into a plunging attack.

The main feature of the Crow Talons, however, is their weapon art, *Raptor Flurry*. When triggered, the wielder will spread their arms before launching forward, gaining Hyper Armor and rapidly unleashing 6 high stagger attacks with high Bleed buildup.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
Sister Friede -  Dark Souls III - boss - second_phase_father_ariandel_and_friede 
 second_phase_father_ariandel_and_friede : After killing Friede in her first phase, a cutscene will play in which Father Ariandel enters a berserk state, expands the arena, resurrects Friede, and begins to fight the player alongside Friede. During this phase, both Father Ariandel and Sister Friede will share the same health bar, and both will die once the health bar is depleted.

Sister Friede will fight much more defensively, opting to cast ice spells from afar instead of directly engaging the player. However, she will still attack if the player gets too close to her.

Father Ariandel fights by using his bowl like a weapon and uses it to try and crush the player. He also has several area of effect attacks that are best avoided by staying either away from him, or behind him. He moves slowly and will charge at the player if they are too far away from him to be hit by any of his attacks.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
Sister Friede -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : Can be parried, backstabbed and riposted.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
Sister Friede -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : **Sister Friede**, born **Elfriede**, is a character and boss in *Dark Souls III*. She is voiced by Amara Karan.

Exclusive to the *Ashes of Ariandel* DLC, she is located in Ariandel Chapel in the Painted World of Ariandel. She can first be talked to as a regular character, and later acts as the final boss of the DLC; her boss battle has three phases, the second of which sees Father Ariandel fight alongside her.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
Sister Friede -  Dark Souls III - boss - location 
 location : Sister Friede is found sitting on a chair in Ariandel Chapel in the Painted World of Ariandel.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
Sister Friede -  Dark Souls III - boss - first_phase_sister_friede 
 first_phase_sister_friede : First of all, it is suggested to use a light weapon (such as a straight sword, a greatsword, etc.) to avoid the risk of being stun-locked by her fast attacks, and also a greatshield with high stability to minimize some stamina damage.

After the beginning of the fight, be careful and learn her attack patterns while blocking with your shield (be careful anyway, because her scythe inflicts Magic damage).

Note that Friede will nearly always jump away after one or two hits, so it is not advised to go for more as it is very easy to disregard stamina and become open for a devastating counterattack. While she seems to have very little poise, she sometimes will almost completely ignore the player's attacks and poise through them with no trouble, guaranteeing the player gets hit if they are getting greedy.

title: Sister Friede

title: Sister Friede

If attacked (including kicking) while she is sitting in her chair, she will disappear until the area is reloaded, and will not mention having been attacked when spoken to in future.
**If she is still absent when opening the path to Father Ariandel, she will also be absent for the cutscene and her voice lines will not be heard. She will, however, reappear when the player talks to Ariandel to start the boss fight.
Blackflame Friede bears several attacks that practically mirror those of Lady Maria, a boss in *Bloodborne*.
Despite having not had contact with Yuria for a long time, and having long abandoned the Sable Church, she, as well as Sir Vilhelm, recognizes the recently anointed Lord of Hollows.

title: Sister Friede
snippet: Friede remained in the chapel of the Painted World, guarding the Flame and Father Ariandel against trespassers, while the inhabitants of the painting rotted and filthy insects spread. When an Ashen One arrived in the painting, she would kindly but firmly invite them to leave and return to the outside world, leaving the inhabitants of the painting in peace and forgetting about them. When they ignored her advice and descended the chapel to confront Father Ariandel, she would be forced to wield her scythe and confront them, not before asking Father Ariandel to turn his gaze away from the imminent carnage. When she is defeated the first time, an enraged Ariandel sparks the Flame he bled so much to subdue, in a desperate attempt to revive her. Now rekindled, Friede would come back from death to fight by his side, their souls linked.  third_phase_blackflame_friede : After defeating the second phase, Friede will resurrect a final time. She will now fight with two scythes. Her original scythe will typically be coated in "Black Flame", and will deal significantly more damage than before. Her secondary scythe will deal heavy frostbite damage, as well as wielding multiple ranged attacks freezing the ground and building up your frost bite meter. However, when the painting began to rot away and its inhabitants made up their minds to burn it, Friede opposed their wish, preferring a slow death in the comforting rot to the renewing change of the Flame. In her second life, Elfriede, now renamed Friede, renounced her past, instead making a home in the Painted World of Ariandel.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
If the Ashen One chooses to ignore Friede and explores the Painted World, they may fight the Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf, which allows the Ashen One to participate in the Undead Match. Deeper inside the painting, the Ashen One finds the Painter, Slave Knight Gael's aforementioned Lady, who has been imprisoned by Friede and Vilhelm in order to prevent her from painting the next world. If the Ashen One opens the way to the inner sanctum hiding Father Ariandel, Friede will confront them and fight to preserve the painting. After a long battle, the Ashen One defeats Friede and Ariandel, prompting the Painted World to begin burning and dooming it to destruction.

The Painter informs the Ashen One that she has sent Gael to find the Dark Soul, which she will use for her next painting.

title: Father Ariandel
snippet:
Father Ariandel -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : Father Ariandel is a large, deformed corvian covered in feathers, with long black hair and a decayed face, similar to other corvians. His head is disproportionately small by comparison to his body, and his limbs are long and thin. He has a deep Scottish accent. Before unlocking the path to him, the sound of him striking himself with his flail can be heard at intervals.

He is bound and tied to a chair where he sinks his head inside a large Lordvessel-like bowl, which he uses as a weapon.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - the_painted_world_of_ariandel 
 the_painted_world_of_ariandel : Within the Cathedral of the Deep the Ashen One can encounter Slave Knight Gael, a Slave Knight who seeks unkindled ash to aid his Lady. Gael presents the Ashen One with a fragment of the Painted World of Ariandel, which sucks the Ashen One in. Within the painting, the Ashen One encounters Sister Friede and her loyal knight Sir Vilhelm. Friede is an advisor to Ariandel, the painting's creator, and convinced him to allow the painting to rot rather than allow it to be destroyed and replaced by a new one, despite the wishes of many of the painting's denizens. Friede bids the Ashen One to leave, telling them that they do not belong in the Painted World.

title: Sir Vilhelm
snippet: His mistress, now known simply as Friede, would gain quite the following among the Corvians who inhabited the painting, including the loyalty of the Corvian Knights and the favor of Father Ariandel himself. Once Sister Friede has been defeated and the player is in possession of her soul, Yuria will remark on Elfriede's history with Londor, and request that the Ashen One usurp the First Flame in her memory.

Should the player have not yet acquired 8 Dark Sigils in either case, the dialogue will vary slightly.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet: However, Corvian society would split when the painting began rotting, just as it had long ago. Most of the settlers wished for the painting to burn like the time before, so that a new one could be restored in its place. Friede, however, couldn't let go of the world that had become her home, convincing Ariandel to bury the flame and enlisting the Corvian Knights to protect the painting from fire. She even had her enforcer, Sir Vilhelm, hide away the Painter who was meant to see flame, just to ensure the world wouldn't be burnt to cinders.

title: Father Ariandel
snippet:
Father Ariandel -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Father Ariandel is the keeper of the Painted World of Ariandel, thought to have been the most recent one to restore it after the Painted World of Ariamis rotted away. When he met the Unkindled Sister Elfriede, she convinced him to forgo the destruction of his rotting world, and to stifle the flame that would burn it to be replaced by a new world by the next restorer, choosing to rot together

He constantly flails himself, bleeding onto the flame, to prevent the fire from burning his world, for he used blood in the restoration, and only that blood could prevent the fire from blazing again. When Friede's blood flows to the bowl containing the flame, the sight of her corpse enrages Father Ariandel, causing him to break free and strike the bowl against her unkindled blood to spark the flame and revive her by restoring her ember as an unkindled.

snippet: The Painted World inhabitants normally followed a custom to preserve the painting against the erosion of time: When their world showed signs of rotting, one that would slowly corrupt and stagnate the entire Painted World, they would "cleanse" it by burning their own home. Father Ariandel, a Great Corvian, was entrusted with the flame with which the Painted World would be burned when the time came; following a collective decision, he would unleash the flame, for the sake of the next Painted World. However, after Friede's arrival, when the world began to wither away due to the rot, she opposed the inhabitants' wish to burn their world, preferring the comforting rot to the cleansing flame. She convinced Ariandel to subdue the flame using his own blood, while Corvian Knights infatuated with Friede "protected" their world, even killing their own brethren who opposed her. The Painter, the "Lady" of the corvians, was imprisoned in the library of the corvian village, to prevent her from

title: The Painter
snippet: In service of her twisted goal, Friede ordered Sir Vilhelm to imprison and guard the Painter in the library of the corvian village to prevent her from restoring the painting. This would prompt Slave Knight Gael to escape from the painting, taking with him a rotten scrap of it and beginning his search for another Unkindled that would fulfill the prophecy, which stated that when the Ashes inside the painting became two, the Flame would return and burn the rot away.

title: Sister Friede
snippet: Following Prince Lothric's refusal to link the First Flame, the Unkindled were exhumed from their graves, tasked with hunting down the Lords of Cinder that had refused to serve once again as kindling. Among the resurrected Unkindled was Elfriede, who instead chose to renounce everything, leaving behind her role as leader of the Sable Church, Londor, and even her name, becoming known simply as "Friede". Left without a home, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, where the forlorn and the outcast were welcomed and found refuge. Friede became the first Ashen One to reside in it, coming to accept the cold of the Painted World and considering it her new home. She discovered that she wanted to "protect" the inhabitants of the Painted World, and thus assumed the precise form that they yearned for: that of their former mistress Priscilla. She went so far as to wield a great scythe, which was symbolic of a long-lost home for the inhabitants of the painting and similar to

Use to acquire numerous souls, or transpose to extract its true strength.

title: Londor
snippet:
At some point before seeing his dream realized, Kaathe died, and left the sisters of the Sable Church to carry on his vision of an Age of Dark led by the Dark Lord.

At some point, Elfriede, as leader of the Sable Church, departed Londor to attempt to link the First Flame. It is uncertain whether she intended to usurp the Flame, bringing the Sable Church's efforts to fruition, or if she wholly abandoned Londor to link the Flame for another purpose (see Sister Friede#Theories). Regardless, she was unable to withstand the Flame's power, and was burned to Ash. Following her failure—and after being resurrected by the Bell of Awakening—Elfriede chose to renounce everything, leaving behind her role as leader of the Sable Church, Londor, and even her name, becoming known simply as "Friede". Having lost her purpose, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel and came to consider it her new home, leaving Yuria and Liliane to carry on the mission of Londor.

title: Sister Friede
snippet: lore : Elfriede is the eldest sister of Yuria and Liliane. The three sisters at one point entered into the service of the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, becoming his maidens. The Primordial Serpent taught them his art of the Dark Hand, which could sap the essence of its victims. The sisters pursued Kaathe's goal of ending the Age of Fire founded by the gods and ushering the Age of Dark, and searched for a Dark Lord who could usurp the First Flame and use its powers to lead the humans into a new age. To this end, the three sisters used their battle prowess to establish the Sable Church, an organization that claimed to offer salvation to Hollows. Elfriede, the eldest sister, became its leader. The Church became a haven for those with unsavory or blurry pasts, along with other rejects of the Age of Fire. An increasing number of Undead and Hollows flocked to the Church, forming a society of wretchedly aged, deceitful, deeply detested Hollows. Their realm would be known as Londor, where

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : Can be parried, riposted and backstabbed in both phases of the encounter.
The Watchers wake up based on a timer. Damage dealt has an effect on how many of them are active.
All Watchers are instantly killed when the first phase of the fight is finished.
The Abyss-corrupted (red-eyed) Watchers are capable of finishing off the main Watcher. This has no direct effect on gameplay, however.
If an enemy followed the player up to the fog door, it may attract the corrupted Watcher's attention and he will keep trying to attack it for the rest of the first phase, rendering him unable to help against the others.
The Watchers that resurrect in the first phase of the fight are actually the same two Watchers, they will resurrect on the spot where they were killed.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet:
Slave Knight Gael -  Dark Souls III - character - notes 
 notes : Gael cannot be permanently killed as a character. He will always respawn in the Cleansing Chapel (may take several reloads).
Gael's summon sign for fighting Sister Friede is unique in that it can be used even if not embered; moreover, he will be summoned directly into the arena, not at his summoning sign, and only when the second phase of the fight commences. He is the only character in the franchise to have a summon sign that functions this way. It also can be used if all your phantom summons are filled up even with the Dried Finger, allowing for a boss fight with 4 phantoms. Furthermore, this summon does not increase Friede's health, similarly to Great Grey Wolf Sif's summon in *Dark Souls I* for Manus, Father of the Abyss.

title: Endurance (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Endurance (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - equipment_load 
 equipment_load : Equipment load determines how much equipment the player can equip before being affected by movement penalties. The softcap for endurance is 40 in terms of carry weight. The Mask of the Father, Havel's Ring, and Ring of Favor and Protection also improve equipment load. Though Mask of the Father is so heavy it usually cancels out its own effect.

title: Chaos Servant
snippet:
Chaos Servant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : After defeating Chaos Witch Quelaag, reach the circular room beneath the Bell of Awakening where there are cobwebs lining eggs on the sides. The wall to the right is illusory. Inside, there will be an egg-infected man named Eingyi. The player must answer "Yes" to his question in order for him to move. If the player has answered "No", quitting and reloading will prompt Eingyi to pose his question again. The player may also kill him and join without repercussion. However, this will cost the player his services. Talking to Quelaag's Sister will give the option to join the covenant.

title: The Painter
snippet: The Painter was brought to the library's attic by Sir Vilhelm, who was guarding her and the key to her chamber. Vilhelm was acting on the orders of Sister Friede, who imprisoned the Painter with Father Ariandel's help. Ariandel is suppressing the Flame of the Painting with his own blood, hence only his and Friede's death can allow the Painter to see Flame. Upon being freed from house arrest, the Painter relocates from the library to the Ariandel Chapel attic. At the attic, she's found sitting in front of a big canvas; when spoken to, she divulges her vision of the new Painting. She emphasizes that the painting will show "a cold, dark, and very gentle place", which is going to be a good home for someone.

title: Dragonrider
snippet:

 attacks : Throughout the boss fight, the attack combos get longer as the Dragonrider's health decreases. There are three different phases (start, middle, and near-end of fight) to the attack patterns based on its health, and the new attacks simply combo after the previous ones. Most of the new attacks are simply extra horizontal swings with a few exceptions. Like most enemies, the combos are only performed if the player is still in range of the attacks.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : Lorian can be parried in both phases of the fight, although he cannot be riposted afterward. However, he can be poise-broken with continuous hits, allowing to perform a riposte on him.
Lothric's "Soul Spear" can be spell-parried, but timing has to be perfect.
If the player manage to complete first phase in position, where Lothric can't see him, they will remain inactive and engage the player only if either provoked or by getting in their line of sight.
If the player is killed or exits the game during the second phase of the battle, they will have to start it again from the first phase on return.

title: Sacred Flame
snippet:

 how_to_obtain : In order to survive the trip inside the lava, there are many strategies that can be followed and even combined before venturing inside. The main idea is to slow down the loss of HP, allowing the player to heal up and advance a bit further, repeating the process as many times as necessary until they have successfully obtained the item.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:

 how_to_join : Talk to Blue Sentinel Targray, located in the Cathedral of Blue directly after the Old Dragonslayer boss fight. Reaching him before obtaining at least one Token of Fidelty will have him disregard the player, so be sure to find one if you wish to join the covenant. Upon meeting the requirements and accepting Targray's offer, players will be awarded the Guardian's Seal.

title: Petrus of Thorolund
snippet:
After the Capra Demon in the lower Undead Burg is defeated, Petrus is joined by Reah of Thorolund and two companions from the Thorolund Order (named Vince and Nico) in the Firelink Shrine. They are on a secret mission and will not talk much about what is going on. Once the game has been reloaded or the player leaves Firelink Shrine, the visitors will be gone and Petrus will not talk much about what happened.

If the player talks to Lautrec of Carim he will offer information to the player for souls based upon level. He tells the player about how the lady and two companions went down to The Catacombs and got attacked, while Petrus escaped and left the others behind. If the player talks to Petrus after this, he will tell his side of the story and about how the lady is left alone and her companions have been turned to hollow.

Talking to Oswald of Carim will result in some implications and accusations against Petrus, claiming that his soul is drenched in sin.

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Brotherhood of Blood -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to Titchy Gren, located in the Undead Purgatory directly after the Executioner's Chariot boss fight. Reaching him before obtaining at least one Token of Spite will have him disregard the player, so be sure to find one if you wish to join the covenant. Upon meeting the requirements and confirming your desire of bathing in blood to Titchy Gren multiple times, players will be awarded the Crest of Blood.

title: Rosaria's Fingers
snippet:
Rosaria's Fingers -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to Saint Rosaria in the Cathedral of the Deep.

title: Painted World of Ariandel
snippet:
Painted World of Ariandel -  Dark Souls III - location - notes 
 notes : There is a giant, two peaked mountain beyond the chapel, nestled in the mountain range. This is the largest mountain that is a part of the "mountain scenery" in the unplayable areas of the game. It can be easily seen from the rope bridge.
A giant, disused bell (comparable in size to the one in the Great Belfry at Archdragon Peak) is on the hillside leading up to the chapel basement.
Stars can be seen in the sky; the same patterns of stars can be seen over Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.
The chapel interior hosts well over a dozen paintings of Sister Friede, in a few different poses. Most appear to be scorched, or in bad condition.
A statue of Crossbreed Priscilla in poor condition is in the back of Sister Friede's boss room, in a small alcove, just beyond the bonfire leading to the Dreg Heap.

title: Old Dragonslayer
snippet:
Old Dragonslayer -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : The fight is very similar to the Dragonslayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough battle without Smough. There are slight differences in how the Old Dragonslayer fights compared to Ornstein. An example would be that the Old Dragonslayer uses a dark magic attack, while Ornstein uses lightning. Otherwise, Old Dragonslayer has the same sort of movement and similar attack patterns as Ornstein in the original *Dark Souls* should the player slay Executioner Smough first. If one takes his time fighting him, he will shoot three dark magic orbs at the player from the tip of his spear.

title: Company of Champions
snippet:
Company of Champions -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : The player can join this covenant as soon as they arrive to Majula. Going between the houses of Lenigrast and Shalquoir, a ledge extending from the cliffside can be found which leads to the Victor's Stone. Upon interacting with the stone, the player must confirm multiple times that they are certain about joining the covenant, and doing so will have them recieve the Champion's Tablet.

title: Way of Blue
snippet:
Way of Blue -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to Crestfallen Saulden, who sits at the base of a tall monument in Majula, four times. Doing so will make him offer the player to join the covenant and accepting will have them recieve the Blue Seal.

title: Giant Mosquito
snippet:
Giant Mosquito -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : Their aggression often leads them to try and navigate to the player even if they are not in clear line of sight. This can lead to situations where they helplessly try to go through a wall or floor to reach you, making them a very easy target as they cannot hit you in this state and can be struck with weaponry given the right angle. Care does need to be taken in the event the mosquito does manage to go past the obstacle towards the player.

title: Undead Supplicant
snippet:
Undead Supplicant -  Dark Souls II - enemy - locations 
 locations : Three are part of the Prowling Magus and Congregation boss fight.

Three dwell beyond the door found above the Rise of the Dead bonfire in Shrine of Amana (the player must be hollowed in order to open this door).

In *Scholar of the First Sin*, they can be found crawling in the two poisonous pits of Harvest Valley.

title: Iudex Gundyr
snippet:
Iudex Gundyr -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : As an Abyssal creature, Gundyr is weak to the Wolf Knight's Greatsword and Farron Greatsword. However, both will be unavailable for the player's first encounter, as they require defeating Abyss Watchers.
Gundyr can be parried and riposted during both phases of the fight.
Gundyr can be staggered. Staggers cannot be followed by a riposte, but Instability damage will be inflicted for the duration of the animation.
Despite appearing similar to the Pus of Man enemies, neither Phase 1 nor Phase 2 are weak to fire.
In shooting Gundyr in the head with a bow during the brief period between him standing and his health bar appearing, Gundyr will be permanently frozen in place and unable to fight back. As such, he can be killed without any real fight.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : First, acquire the Darkmoon Seance Ring in The Catacombs. Go to the bottom level of the rotating elevator in Anor Londo to find the Darkmoon Tomb bonfire. Past the bonfire, Gwyn's statue will disappear to reveal a fog gate if the player is wearing the Darkmoon Seance Ring. If the player has killed Gwynevere, the statue will just disappear when approached. Go toward the fog gate and Dark Sun Gwyndolin will ask the player to swear fealty to the Blades of the Darkmoon. Kneel at the fog door to join the covenant.

title: Messages
snippet:
Messages -  Dark Souls - mechanic - rating 
 rating : Along with the text contents of the message, messages have a rating. Messages can be rated using either the Orange Guidance Soapstone or the gesture button. A positive (+) or negative (-) rating can be given based on if the player found the message helpful or not. The rating shows how many times this message has been rated, but not how many of these rating were positive or negative. The player can only see the composition of ratings while using Seek Guidance. Developer messages can not be rated.

Ratings also determine the image that accompanies it. How many ratings a message has received will change the icon it uses.

title: Clawed Curse
snippet:
Clawed Curse -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : Grand Archives Scholars have their own heads covered in wax to protect themselves from these specters. They tend the many vats filled with this liquid found throughout the library.
In the official guide, there is a description for the Scholar's Shed Skin telling how "ivory wax" is made to prevent your "anchor of reason" from being damaged by the "foulness" of the texts. How this works in relation to the curse effect they give is not clear, but they could represent how the mind interprets the harm they do, though how exactly this harms people is uncertain.
They share a resemblance with the arm that appears out of the Curse-rotted Greatwood in its second phase.

title: White Hair Talisman
snippet:
White Hair Talisman -  Dark Souls III - weapon - how_to_obtain 
 how_to_obtain : In order to survive the trip inside the lava, there are many strategies that can be followed and even combined before venturing inside. The main idea is to slow down the loss of HP enough time, allowing the player to heal up and advance a bit further, repeating the process as many times as necessary until they have successfully gotten the item and returned to solid ground. Each time the player's health reaches half of the HP bar, they should heal.

title: Dragon Remnants
snippet:
Dragon Remnants -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to Magerold of Lanafir in Iron Keep, who will beg the player to be given the Petrified Egg if it's in their inventory. Giving him the treasure will allow players to enter the Dragon Remnants covenant, and they recieve an Ancient Dragon Seal and a Dragon Eye upon joining.

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Bell Keepers -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : To join the Bell Keepers, the player must speak to the Bell Keeper of Alken at the entrance of Belfry Luna or Belfry Sol. Exhausting his dialogue will allow the player to join the covenant and accepting will have them recieve the Bell Keeper's Seal.

title: Way of White
snippet:
Way of White -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Players may join the Way of White by talking either to Petrus at the Firelink Shrine or Reah after you have rescued her from the Tomb of the Giants.

Players who choose to be in the Knight class or the Cleric class begin the game already in the Way of White. (Though this does not unlock the trophy/achievement for discovering the Way of White covenant. Unlocking the trophy/achievement as a knight or cleric will require abandoning the covenant and then re-joining via talking to Petrus or Reah).

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : There are two phases to this fight: the "chariot" phase and the "horse" phase.

As you enter the fog door, phase one begins. The chariot will circle around the arena and attempt to ram into you. This can be avoided by hiding in the openings along the walls, or with a well-timed roll. The corridor is littered with Skeletons that will continue to revive until the Necromancers, which are hiding in the gaps along the walls, are killed. The chariot progressively loses speed the more damage it is dealt, giving you more time between its laps to deal with the skeletons and necromancers.

title: Large Soul of a Crestfallen Knight
snippet:
Large Soul of a Crestfallen Knight -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : A total of six can be found in each playthrough. Three are found in the base game, one in *Ashes of Ariandel* and two in *The Ringed City*:

Grand Archives
**On the fifth floor of the library, in the area with four Grand Archives Scholars. The item is at the other end of the central bookshelves, where several Clawed Curses spawn.
**In the big courtyard past the roofs section, where Lion Knight Albert, Black Hand Kamui and Daughter of Crystal Kriemhild attack the player. The soul can be looted from a corpse right before the encounter.

Archdragon Peak
** Past the Great Belfry, there is a large courtyard with ruins and numerous Man Serpents. The item is found on a corpse close to Hawkwood the Deserter's summon sign.

title: Channeler
snippet:
Channeler -  Dark Souls - enemy - locations 
 locations : In the Undead Parish church, just before the Bell Gargoyles, on a ledge surrounded by sword-wielding Hollows. Does not respawn.
In the Depths above the Gaping Dragon boss entrance. This Channeler will buff the Gaping Dragon if he is not eliminated first, making the fight considerably harder. Does not respawn.
Three in The Duke's Archives. The first is located after the first lift. The other two are positioned in consecutive levels, above the bonfire on the balcony.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet: fight_overview : When encountered as a boss, Gael appears monstrous and his moves mirror his beastly nature, he does high amounts of damage and can endure some significant punishment himself. Aside from the damage his moveset has him bounding, and jumping around the players position in a manner that can even force the lock-on function to drop. His attacks are all easy to memorize however, and the only time the player should worry is when Gael rears back, releases a frustrated groan, quickly followed by several powerful strikes. Followed at the end by high leap plunge attack that affects a small area around the blades impact. Key to this battle is his poise, he can be staggered but not riposted, the player should pay close attention to how many hits it takes to stagger him (usually three with great weapons), and act accordingly, if this weakness exploited correctly he can be stunned out of his hard-hitting combos in the second phase.
